reason: The text explicitly describes the Israelites suffering under Egyptian slavery ('they made their lives bitter with hard labor'), but attributes this suffering to Egyptian oppression rather than to any fault of the Israelites. The text presents no evidence of Israelite wrongdoing causing their bondage. Instead, it portrays them as innocent victims whose groaning God hears and whose covenant God remembers, leading to divine intervention for their deliverance. God sends Moses to liberate them from oppression, not to punish them for their own transgressions.
